data.name: Cleansuit
data.detailed_description:
Cleansuit is a retro-style graphical text adventure game where you must find creative ways to survive a mysterious serial killer's assault on your home. Use text commands to manipulate the detailed environment and discover all the unique ways to win and die.

Become the schlubby protagonist who must outwit his would-be killer: Explore your home, collect items to devise a path to survival, and cheat death. Along the way you'll find secrets hidden through your house. Some may help you. Most are lethal.

What will you need to make it out alive? Bring your ingenuity, your curiosity, and most of all your will to live!

reviews.review:
Cleansuit is a horror title that basks in the niche sub-genre of oldschool text-based adventures; though it does come with a modernized graphical twist. You take on the role of an average Joe who is home alone at night, when all of a sudden there is a knock at the door. Answering it head on just might be your first of many deaths, as you attempt to outwit the mysterious Cleansuit Killer.

Unlike many older text-based adventure games, Cleansuit is very easy to navigate. The game only responds to a handful of commands, and most of the items that you can interact with are denoted in the descriptive text of each room. The real challenging part is figuring out which objects to combine and where to place them. There's a lot of trial and error to be had, but once you start figuring out what to do the game goes by fairly quickly. There are even some secrets to find, Easter Eggs to enjoy, and laughs to be had.

In total, there are five main endings with seven variation twists; meaning that you can replay certain end sequences, but figure out different ways of killing the killer, or how to get him captured. They're all worth working toward, although the variations usually aren't that big of an outcome changer. The really fun part, for me at least, is figuring out all of the ways that you can be killed. There are far more self-deaths than there are killer-deaths, and a lot of them are hilarious; for instance, try typing in "jerk off" repeatedly.

Despite the tongue-in-cheek nature of Cleansuit, the game itself does have a decently creepy atmosphere. The fact that you're unsure of when the killer will appear next keeps your blood pumping, and creates a sense of urgency in your movements. If you're down for a great little dark comedy title with subtle hints of horror, then Cleansuit is the modernized text-based adventure that you've been waiting for. The hour/hour and a half long content is definitely worth the $4.65 CAD. If you're looking for something that's more serious but within the same sub-genre, check out Dark Fear.

[h1]Rating: [b]4.5/5.0[/b] - Excellent, highly worth playing.[/h1]
